class: A decision that belongs to the owner had no place to live except as a loosened rule
symptom: A Discipline list offered "Computer Science" but not the owner's "Computer Technology"; the agent (correctly, by its own rule) left the box empty, and the owner asked why it could not use the near match.
root_cause: The rule that a field of study is never swapped for another subject protects what the owner certifies, but gave the owner no way to say "this substitute is fine": the only options were a blank box or loosening the rule for everyone and every value.
why_tests_missed: The tests pinned the refusal to substitute; nothing modelled an owner who approves a specific substitute.
fix: profile.answer_alternatives (the owner's data, e.g. {"Computer Technology": ["Computer Science"]}): after the exact value is not offered, choose() tries only the alternatives the owner listed, in order; the hand-over says when one was used; apply_answers records what was chosen so the check that an answer stayed does not loop. Nothing else is substituted, and the exact value always wins.
prevention: When a safety rule refuses something the owner may legitimately want, give the owner a data-level way to approve exactly that case (per value, ordered, reported at hand-over) rather than loosening the rule.
